description: SSH, SFTP, databases, monitoring, backups, updates and remote desktops for your own servers from ChatGPT, keyless through the Termalin Connector, with skills for server health, alert triage, safe commands, deploy checks, databases, backups, security updates, new server setup, internal web services and RDP/VNC desktops.

interface.longDescription:
Termalin lets ChatGPT work on the Linux servers, VPS and cloud machines you connect. It can run commands over SSH, read and write files over SFTP, query your databases and read your server monitoring. You never paste an SSH key or password into ChatGPT.

To start, sign in at termal.in and install a Termalin Connector on a server with one command: https://termal.in/account

You can ask ChatGPT to:
• Check disk and memory, tail a log, restart a service, edit a config, install a package.
• Find what is filling the disk and run a migration in the background.
• Run one command on several servers at once.
• List tables and run queries on Postgres, MySQL and other databases.
• Read metrics and alerts: CPU, memory, disk, load, failed services, certificates.
• Check and run encrypted backups, and set up a fresh VPS.
• List pending security updates and CVEs and install them with your approval.
• Open an internal dashboard such as Grafana without opening a port, and work on Windows (RDP) or Linux and Mac (VNC) desktops.

How access works: your servers connect outward through the Connector, so no inbound port is open. Each command is authenticated with a short-lived certificate. ChatGPT connects through OAuth from your termal.in account after you approve it. Your keys, passwords and tokens stay on your side, and the chat only receives command output.

You stay in control: set each connection to full access, an allowlist of commands, or read-only. Add a note on each server to tell the AI what to be careful with. Every command is logged, and you can disconnect in one click from your account page.
